answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake before it can submit work, then slash that stake when independent reviewers confirm fraud. Because one attacker creating a thousand accounts must lock up a thousand stakes, fake identities become costly rather than nearly free; the attacker also risks losing capital for each detected account. The harbor marketplace can release honest stakes after review, while a comet-like burst of new accounts triggers slower checks, with cedar nodes sampling submissions across identities to catch coordinated abuse.
